_comment: Mutation sweep for V-CTN-038 -- authority never precedes machinery (07 §5), invariant 7 of dev/tests/invariants-gate.py. Run: python3 dev/mutate.py verification/mutants/V-CTN-038.json. Every row names the test that must fail; see dev/mutate.py for why rc != 0 is not a catch. This arm is the one arm of the gate whose ENFORCING BRANCH the tree has never executed: no agent identity holds a write verb today, so `if not absent: continue` is reached on every run and the finding below it on none. Mutating the branch is the only way to establish that a green here is the property holding rather than the input being absent.

mutants.why: THE defect the class exists for. With the arm gone a tree that lost its tier labels -- or a `kind: Role` regex that stopped matching -- returns [] and prints the same green tick as a tree whose grants are all read-only. [[LSN-035]]: in this repo VACUOUS is a failure, and the only way to keep it one is to run the empty corpus.

The dangerous spelling, and it is dangerous precisely NOW: from Phase 9 on all four machinery items exist, so `not docs and missing_machinery()` is false for an empty corpus and the gate reports green on a tree that can no longer see any agent RBAC. Deliberately invisible to M1's catcher, which supplies absent machinery.

edits.replace:
if not docs and missing_machinery():
        return [

mutants.why: `if True: continue` is what the code already does on every real run, made unconditional. A write verb on an agent identity with no undo path -- the exact situation 07 §5 forbids -- then produces no output at all.

The other end of the same line. Invariant 7 is about ORDER: a write verb is legal once the machinery is there, and Phase 10 grants one. A gate that fails on every write verb regardless would have to be deleted rather than satisfied, and it would read as green-and-strict until the day it blocked correct work.
Over-reporting is the loud direction, but it is also the direction that gets a gate switched off: every reader ServiceAccount in the tree would fail invariant 7 while the machinery is being built.

`*` is the single most dangerous grant and the one a set-membership test is most likely to be wrong about. Adding it to READ_VERBS lets `verbs: ["*"]` through while `patch` is still caught, so every other control in the class stays green.

The finding is what a human acts on. Naming one of three missing items sends them to build one thing and re-run into the same red, which is how a correct gate acquires a reputation for moving the goalposts.

edits.find: f"makes a write survivable does not exist: {', '.join(absent)}. "
edits.replace: f"makes a write survivable does not exist: {absent[0]}. "

mutants.why: `agent_rbac_documents()` scans the whole tree including templates. A finding that names the verb but not the file leaves the reader grepping for which of them granted it, and the answer may be a `.yaml.template` that only exists after envsubst.

mutants.why: [[LSN-035]] in its narrow form: a control that only asks whether the list is non-empty cannot tell which property fired. The 07 §5 citation is what makes this finding distinguishable from the other fifteen the gate can emit.
